newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FACE INNINGS DEFEAT VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FACE INNINGS DEFEAT VS NZ.

text.p: Sri Lanka had their backs to the wall on Monday after losing four second-innings wickets on the fourth day of the first cricket test against New Zealand.
Sri Lanka were 102 for four at the lunch break, with captain Arjuna Ranatunga on four and Hashan Tillekaratne on one.
The tourists resumed on 37 without loss, needing a further 327 runs to make New Zealand bat a second time.
New Zealand amassed 586 for seven declared in their first innings and Sri Lanka replied with a disappointing 222.

Sri Lanka's hopes of saving the game with a big second innings were dealt a series of blows in the morning session when they lost openers Roshan Mahanama for 21, Sanath Jayasuriya for 50, dangerman Aravinda de Silva for nought and Marvan Atapattu for 22.
De Silva, the third man to depart with the score on 85, was the victim of a questionable leg-before-wicket decision.
The delivery, from medium-paced change bowler Nathan Astle, pitched outside off stump and looked on television replays to be moving further away when it struck de Silva's back pad.
Mahanama and Jayasuriya were both dismissed by fast-medium bowler Simon Doull, who had collected two for 46 by the break to add to his five for 58 in the Sri Lankan first innings.
Mahanama played a big inside edge on to his stumps, while Jayasuriya chased the ball outside offstump and was caught behind immediately after raising his fifth test half-century off 68 balls.
Atapattu departed in the penultimate over before lunch. He attempted to sweep offspinner Dipak Patel only to drag the ball on to his stumps.
